articles.body:
The ESPN fantasy basketball experts got together for their second mock draft of the 2026-27 NBA season, using a 10-team roto format.

If you're new to fantasy hoops and looking to try it out for the first time, here is a tutorial of all the basics. From there, it's easy to grab a handful of people, set up a draft and have some fun! Before that, though, it's always smart to spend a little time preparing with a mock draft of your own.

When it comes to roto and category leagues, certain players can be ranked differently than points leagues. In particular, that's true of players who excel in some stat categories or, on the flip side, are below average in some categories.

So how far did Giannis Antetokounmpo's poor free throw shooting cause him to fall? Where did Tyrese Haliburton go after missing a full season because of injury?

articles.headline: Where has Bears TE Colston Loveland been this season?
articles.description: The tight end has one catch and faces a tough Eagles defense on MNF. With no Caleb Williams, can he get going?
articles.headlineJa: ベアーズのTEコルストン・ラブランドは今季どうしたのか？
articles.descriptionJa: ここまでわずか1キャッチにとどまっているタイトエンドは、MNFで強力なイーグルス守備陣と対戦します。ケイレブ・ウィリアムズ不在の中、調子を取り戻せるでしょうか？
articles.body:
The day before the Chicago Bears hosted the Minnesota Vikings in their home opener Sept. 20, The Wiener's Circle -- a famous Chicago hot dog stand -- offered free dogs if Bears tight end Colston Loveland scored two touchdowns.

Bears fans were unable to cash in as Loveland finished with just one catch -- not a TD -- for 3 yards. Fantasy managers also have been unable to cash in with Loveland, who was the No. 3 tight end drafted -- after the Arizona Cardinals' Trey McBride and the Las Vegas Raiders' Brock Bowers -- but is being started in only 48% of ESPN leagues heading into Monday's game against the Philadelphia Eagles (8:15 p.m. ET, ABC/ESPN).

Loveland's 3-yard catch in the 9-3 loss to the Vikings was his only reception on five targets this season, and that includes a 59-37 win against the Carolina Panthers in Week 1. That's not what was expected from last year's No. 10 overall pick out of Michigan who led the NFC North champs with 713 receiving yards and 58 receptions.

"Everyone in here wants the ball," Loveland said. "We're here for a reason, and we want to make plays and help our team win.

"But there's other ways to make plays on the ground in the run game. I'm just doing what I'm asked. There's going to be opportunities, so I've just got to take full advantage when it arises."

Could those opportunities come against the Eagles? Philadelphia's defense has allowed the third-fewest receptions (six) and second-fewest receiving yards (42) and is tied for the third-fewest targets faced against tight ends (nine) after wins against the Washington Commanders and Tennessee Titans.

"It's kind of a bit of a chess match knowing he's a guy that can take off at any moment because that's what he did last year," Eagles linebacker Chance Campbell said.

Loveland averaged 597 receiving yards over his final 10 games last season. He was a favorite target of Caleb Williams, but the quarterback will be inactive Monday night because of a hamstring injury. Case Keenum will start.

Keenum threw Loveland his first TD of a training camp that served as a daily highlight reel for the tight end. The offseason seemed to foreshadow another season of high usage in coach Ben Johnson's offense.

Instead, it has been just the opposite.

Loveland's disappearance is multifaceted. Offensive coordinator Press Taylor and Johnson are adamant Loveland is built into the game plan, often as the primary receiver. The ball just has yet to find him.

Loveland has been on the field for 86.6% of the Bears' offensive snaps through two games -- the highest of any offensive player other than Williams or a lineman.

"We had plenty of opportunities against Carolina, just couldn't quite feed them the way we wanted to," Johnson said.

Against a Vikings defense that sent a blitz at Williams on 78% of his dropbacks, Loveland and other tight ends were called on to max protect on a rainy afternoon when wet conditions affected the passing game.

articles.headline: Which Premier League players got injured in the international break?
articles.description: All the latest news and updates on Premier League stars injuries during the first international break of the 2026-2027 club season
articles.headlineJa: 代表ウィーク中に負傷したプレミアリーグの選手は？
articles.descriptionJa: 2026-2027クラブシーズンの最初の代表ウィーク期間中に発生したプレミアリーグ主力選手の負傷に関する最新ニュースとアップデート。
articles.body:
Premier League teams will be watching and hoping their star players remain healthy throughout the international break.

However, some have already sustained injuries while playing for their countries. Premier League matches resume on Oct. 10.

ESPN will be tracking the latest injuries and updates for your club's players:

Kai Havertz (Arsenal)

Arsenal's Kai Havertz was forced off in the 30th minute of the game between Netherlands and Germany on September 24th with what was described as a muscle injury.

"Both are currently undergoing an MRI," Jurgen Klopp said on RTL about Havertz and Jamal Musiala. "I hope we get the diagnosis [on Thursday] evening. But of course, this isn't great. I hope it's nothing serious. The lads are probably out for us. But hopefully, they'll be back in action relatively quickly."

On September 25 the German Football Association confirmed the attacker would be leaving Klopp's camp and return to Arsenal after suffering what they describe as a 'muscle strain.'

Brian Brobbey (Sunderland)

The powerful Sunderland attacker was also injured in the same game after picking up what looked like a hamstring injury while running for the ball. He immediately went down and signalled to the sideline.

He left the field of his own accord but did have a heavy limp as he walked down the tunnel.

Netherlands boss Xavi Hernandez said after the game: "Brian is indeed injured."

Brobbey was replaced by Joshua Zirkzee in the Dutch squad.

Zion Suzuki (Aston Villa)

The goalkeeper linked up with the Japan squad but according to reports missed the main group training session on September 22nd, according to local reports. Instead he was put on an individual session for a rib injury.

Suzuki was subsequently left out of Japan's matchday squad entirely for Thursday's 3-1 victory over Uruguay.

Dan Ballard (Sunderland)

The Sunderland defender suffered a reported hamstring injury during Northern Ireland's 1-0 victory over Georgia in the UEFA Nations League.

With the score still 0-0 as the match moved into stoppage time, Ballard chased back as Georgia counter-attacked and pulled up clutching the back of his thigh, unable to finish the match in Tbilisi.

Speaking immediately after Friday's match, manager Michael O'Neill said it was too soon to know the extent of his latest injury but will definitely miss the next three Northern Ireland games.

"We'll scan him tomorrow (Saturday), but he's certainly not going to be available for the next three games."

Alexander Isak (Liverpool)

Alexander Isak is returning to Liverpool after sustaining a "minor injury" on international duty.

The striker scored and played the full 90 minutes in Sweden's 2-1 victory over Romania in the Nations League on Friday.

But Isak, who has made a strong start to the season for Liverpool, will not feature in matches against Poland, Bosnia and Herzegovina and Romania over the remainder of the extended international break.

articles.headline: 2027 NFL draft order projections for Round 1, top pick, more
articles.description: ESPN's Football Power Index projects the 2027 NFL draft order for Round 1, complete with each team's chances to pick in the top five, in the top 10 and at No. 1.
articles.headlineJa: 2027年NFLドラフト第1巡の指名順予想、全体1位指名権など
articles.descriptionJa: ESPNのフットボール・パワー・インデックス（FPI）が2027年NFLドラフト第1巡の指名順を予想。各チームのトップ5、トップ10、全体1位指名権を獲得する確率を網羅しています。
articles.body:
The 2027 NFL draft is still months away, but with the 2026 season underway, we're starting to track pick order in Round 1. Which teams are in position to add elite prospects in the top 10 next April? What about the top five ... or even at No. 1?

What follows is not the current draft order based on records. It is a projection of what ESPN's Football Power Index thinks the order ultimately will be by the end of the season. Each week during the season, the FPI projects the draft order by simulating the remainder of the season 10,000 times. Game probabilities are based primarily on the model's team ratings and game locations. The draft order is determined by the records the model projects for each team after 17 games, as well as each team's average draft position across the simulations.

So where do things stand? Here are the full sortable projections, complete with each team's chances to pick in the top five, in the top 10 and at No. 1.

See more on the NFL draft

First-round picks that have been traded:

The Green Bay Packers' selection was dealt to the Dallas Cowboys in the Micah Parsons trade.

The Indianapolis Colts' selection was dealt to the New York Jets in the Sauce Gardner trade.

The Los Angeles Rams' selection was dealt to the Cleveland Browns in the Myles Garrett trade.

The better of Dallas' two selections (either its own pick or the Packers' original pick) was dealt to the Jets in the Quinnen Williams trade.

articles.headline: Eagles' DeVonta Smith is headed into another stratosphere
articles.description: The Eagles' go-to guy in key moments has always seen himself as WR1 -- now everyone else is just catching up.
articles.headlineJa: イーグルスのデボンテ・スミス、さらなる高みへ
articles.descriptionJa: 勝負どころでイーグルスの頼れる存在である彼は、常に自身をエースWR（WR1）と見なしてきましたが、今や周囲もようやくその評価に追いつきつつあります。
articles.body:
THE PHILADELPHIA EAGLES' offense stepped onto the field in Week 2 down three on the road against the Tennessee Titans with 1:56 remaining. It was the kind of moment, receiver DeVonta Smith said immediately following the game, that "you live for."

Quarterback Jalen Hurts went to Smith four times on the drive. Four times Smith delivered, including on a sideline throw in which Smith stood on his toes and fully extended his arms to snag the ball at a 45-degree angle on his way to the ground. Tap-tap. First down. 

Then came the money play: third-and-6 from the Titans' 22. Hurts zipped one down the left side for Smith, who leapt and stretched high to catch the ball, pivoted away from an oncoming defender in midair, somehow, and managed to drag his feet in bounds as a pair of Titans players crashed on top of him -- a picturesque 19-yard completion that set the stage for Darius Cooper's game-winning touchdown. 

"I take a lot of pride in it," Smith said of being the go-to guy in key moments. There was a short pause. 

"I feel like it was time," he continued, fresh off a 10-catch, 117-yard performance. "It was time for me to go out there and show what I can do, that I can be that guy. I had the opportunity and I went out there and did it."

The subtext here is Smith and the Eagles are now operating in the post-A.J. Brown world. Smith and Brown shined during their four years together, becoming the first Eagles duo to each post 1,000-plus receiving yards in a single season in 2022, then they did it again in '23 and '25. The franchise's all-time postseason receiving yards leader, Smith has hardly been stuck in the shadows. 

But he has long been the 1B to Brown's 1A. Working alongside another alpha receiver in a run-centric system, the volume and production have always been just a tick below superstar status. He has never been an All-Pro or selected to a Pro Bowl. Now in Year 6, the 2020 Heisman Trophy winner finds himself at the center of a revamped passing offense under new coordinator Sean Mannion, backed by an organization that has expressed full confidence both publicly and behind the scenes that Smith is headed to another stratosphere. 

After all, from his game-winning catch in the College Football Playoff National Championship game as a freshman at Alabama in 2017 to hauling in "The Dagger" against the Kansas City Chiefs in Super Bowl LIX, he has matched just about every big moment he has faced.  

Despite his stoic public demeanor and team-first approach, Smith has always seen himself as a true No. 1, Eagles receivers coach Aaron Moorehead said, and now has the opportunity to show the rest of the world why.

"He's not selfish, but he's fiery and feisty," his high school receivers coach Christopher Gordon said. "He's always been that guy, to where it's 'Give me the ball.' You know, 'I'm gonna make a play.'"

articles.headline: Chiefs' Mahomes perfect on play-action passes in win vs. Dolphins
articles.description: Mahomes completed all 14 of his play-action attempts for 201 yards, including a touchdown, according to ESPN Research.
articles.headlineJa: チーフスのマホームズ、ドルフィンズ戦の勝利でプレイアクションパスを完璧に成功
articles.descriptionJa: ESPNリサーチによると、マホームズは14回のプレイアクションパスの試みすべてを成功させ、1タッチダウンを含む201ヤードを獲得しました。
articles.body:
MIAMI GARDENS, Fla. -- Patrick Mahomes' opening snap in Sunday's game against the Miami Dolphins was perhaps his easiest pass of the season.

Mahomes, the Kansas City Chiefs' quarterback, took the snap under center and executed a play-action fake with running back Kenneth Walker III. When Mahomes released the ball, not a single defender was close to tight end Travis Kelce, who turned his wide-open catch into a 48-yard gain.

For the remainder of the game, a 24-10 win for the Chiefs, Mahomes found teammate after teammate open for completion after completion on play-action passes. In total, Mahomes completed all 14 of his play-action attempts for 201 yards, including a touchdown, according to ESPN Research. He also tied Russell Wilson (in 2020) for the most completions without an incompletion on play-action in the past 20 seasons.

"It's helping out a ton," Mahomes said of the Chiefs' play-action attack. "I think people look at the stats and they see the touchdowns that Kenneth has and [rookie running back Emmett Johnson] when they're running the ball. But I don't think they really understand how the play-action and the movements [within the pocket] is really opened up in our offense. That's a credit to [the running backs] and the offensive line firing off the ball, run and pass.

"I thought we did a great job with that."

Last season, the Chiefs, who finished with a disappointing 6-11 record and missed the playoffs for the first time since 2014, were one of the NFL's worst when using play-action. In 178 play-action snaps, the seventh most in the league, the Chiefs recorded just 977 passing yards from, ranking 20th, according to ESPN Research. The Chiefs even surrendered more sacks (nine) than they scored touchdowns (three).

Coach Andy Reid hired Eric Bieniemy in late January to be the new offensive coordinator -- a role he held with the team from 2018 to 2022. In March, during the NFL's free agency period, general manager Brett Veach made the Chiefs' biggest offseason acquisition in signing Walker to a three-year, $43.05 million contract, including $28.7 million fully guaranteed.

After Sunday's game, Mahomes has 329 passing yards, four touchdowns and one interception on play-action attempts. He also hasn't been sacked in 38 such snaps, according to TruMedia.

Throughout the Chiefs' locker room Sunday, several offensive players praised Walker and Bieniemy for creating advantageous opportunities for larger passing gains.

"It's opening up a lot, just knowing our run game has a huge impact," receiver Rashee Rice said. "When it's time for [pass catchers] to be called to make the play downfield when it looks like a run, we have to make that play."

The opening snap was a perfect example. The Chiefs lined up with three tight ends and just two players -- Kelce and receiver Tyquan Thornton -- went out for a route. articles.headline: Joe Burrow, Bengals can't 'close it out' against Steelers
articles.description: Special teams gaffes and a Burrow fumble late in the fourth sealed Cincinnati's outcome.
articles.headlineJa: ジョー・バロウとベンガルズ、スティーラーズ相手に「逃げ切れず」
articles.descriptionJa: スペシャルチームのミスと第4クォーター終盤のバロウのファンブルが、シンシナティの敗戦を決定づけました。
articles.body:
CINCINNATI -- Slightly hunched forward and still mostly in his game attire, Cincinnati Bengals quarterback Joe Burrow sat and stared at the inside of his locker as he pondered a game that slipped away.

The Pittsburgh Steelers (2-1) halted Cincinnati's strong start to the season with a 30-27 victory on Sunday at Acrisure Stadium. And as Burrow pondered what went wrong in a game Cincinnati (2-1) came close to winning, the theme of self-inflicted mistakes jumped out more than anything else.

And as the Week 3 loss showed, those types of errors can be the undoing of a team with championship aspirations.

"Like last week with the penalties, we just can't shoot ourselves in the foot like that," Burrow said. "You can't win in this league when you do that. It's really hard. It's really hard. We could have overcome it, but it's hard to win like that."

Cincinnati was looking to start the season with three wins for the first time since Zac Taylor took over as the team's coach in 2019. Against Houston in Week 2, the Bengals won despite being called for 12 penalties.

One week later, the mistakes by the entire team were too costly.

A Bengals defense that had big moments in the season's first two games surrendered 411 yards to a Pittsburgh squad that failed to score a touchdown a week earlier. Special teams had two major blunders: a roughing-the-kicker penalty that extended a drive culminating in a touchdown and a muffed punt recovered by the Steelers.

That fumbled punt led to Chris Boswell's 33-yard field goal with 2:15 left that proved to be the winning margin.

"We just didn't close it out," Taylor said. "That's all there is to it. We had opportunities in all three phases in the fourth quarter. We didn't get it done."

That includes the offense.

Following Boswell's field goal, Cincinnati got the ball back and still had two timeouts. The Bengals worked into kicker Evan McPherson's range when disaster struck.

After Steelers defensive tackle Derrick Harmon got a quick pressure, Burrow wriggled out of a potential sack and tried to throw the ball away. But Harmon recovered and knocked the ball loose before Burrow could get rid of it, leading to a fumble the Steelers recovered to ice the game.

"Trying to take a shot at the end zone," Burrow said of his final play. "Trying not to take the sack, trying to get the ball out. Fumbled it."

It unspooled an otherwise sterling day from Cincinnati's star quarterback -- 28-of-37 passing for 282 yards and three touchdowns, including one on fourth down that put Cincinnati ahead 27-24 with 13:29 left.

And it also uncovered another trend that has been lurking over the years. Dating to the start of the 2024 season, Burrow is tied for the league lead in lost turnovers in the fourth quarter or overtime, per ESPN Research. He has thrown eight interceptions and lost four fumbles in that span.

articles.body:
Manchester City striker Erling Haaland and future City midfielder Cavan Sullivan are being tracked by Real Madrid and Barcelona amid the club's legal issues, while Arsenal and Spurs will fight for Bayer Leverkusen attacking midfielder Ibrahim Maza. Join us for the latest transfer news and rumors from around the globe.

Transfers home page | Men's summer grades | Women's grades

Trending rumors

- Real Madrid and Barcelona are looking at Manchester City striker Erling Haaland due to uncertainty created by the case surrounding City's financial rule breaches, according to The Sun. A potential points deduction severe enough to cause relegation could raise major questions over the future of key players, including Haaland, who currently has around eight years remaining on his contract. Sport also reports the situation could cast doubt on Cavan Sullivan's move to the Etihad, with the 16-year-old USMNT and Philadelphia Union midfielder having agreed a transfer when he turns 18. Barcelona and Real Madrid are once again the two clubs linked.

- Arsenal and Tottenham Hotspur have stepped up their interest in Bayer Leverkusen attacking midfielder Ibrahim Maza, TEAMtalk reports. Chelsea, Manchester City, and Aston Villa are also attentively monitoring the 20-year-old, whose versatility and technical quality have made him one of the most highly regarded talents in the Bundesliga.

- Arsenal and Chelsea have shown the most Premier League interest in Como center back Jacobo Ramón, according to Diario AS. Real Madrid are considering re-signing the 21-year-old for next season, but the defender prefers to remain at the Italian club to secure regular first-team minutes.

- Barcelona are eyeing RB Leipzig's David Raum and Crystal Palace's Tyrick Mitchell as potential left back options for next summer, reports Diario Sport. With Alejandro Balde struggling for game time and considering his future, the Catalan club continue to evaluate targets to reinforce the position and are looking to take advantage of the fact the pair will be free agents.

- Internazionale, AC Milan, and Juventus are monitoring contract renewal negotiations between Napoli and midfielder André-Frank Zambo Anguissa, according to Tuttosport. Discussions to extend the 30-year-old's contract beyond its 2027 expiration have hit a standstill, while recurring injury concerns limited him to just 18 Serie A appearances last season.

articles.headline: Man City vs. Premier League: 115 financial charges explained
articles.description: The sporting world is waiting for a resolution to the hearings on Man City's charges for allegedly breaching the Premier League's financial rules. Here's what we know, and what might come next.
articles.headlineJa: マンチェスター・シティ vs プレミアリーグ：115件の財務違反疑惑を解説
articles.descriptionJa: スポーツ界は、プレミアリーグの財務ルール違反疑惑をめぐるマンチェスター・シティの聴聞会の決着を待っています。現在分かっていることと、今後の展開について解説します。
articles.body:
Editor's Note: This was originally published March 19, 2025. We have republished and updated this explainer of the facts -- the charges levied against Manchester City and the potential punishments -- along with insight as to the duration of the proceedings in light of Friday's news reports, which City are denying at this time. This is another explainer, from February 2026, shining light on why the process is taking so long.

What are the charges against Manchester City?

They relate to the seasons between 2009-10 and 2022-23 and cover a range of alleged breaches -- the most serious being false accounting, with respect to providing accurate financial information on revenue (including sponsorship revenue), related parties and operating costs. There are other alleged breaches, including irregularities in player and manager remuneration and, in more recent seasons, failure to cooperate with the Premier League's investigation.

If the charges relate to alleged breaches, why are they coming to light only now?

Because much of this issue relates to the "Football Leaks," when internal documents -- "leaked" say the perpetrators, "stolen or false" say some of the victims -- relating to a range of soccer-related issues were made public. German newsmagazine Der Spiegel had access to the cache of documents -- including internal emails -- and published stories accusing Manchester City of flouting financial fair play rules, which regulate how clubs can generate revenue. This led to investigations by UEFA and, later, by the Premier League.

In February 2020, UEFA's investigation found Manchester City guilty and banned them from European football for two seasons while fining them €30 million. The ban was overturned five months later by the Court of Arbitration for Sport on the basis that some charges had exceeded the statute of limitations and others were "not established" by UEFA. City were also fined €10 million for failing to cooperate with the investigation.

Why is the Premier League's case taking so long?

It's a combination of the league's own rules and the many legal challenges City have brought over the years, contesting jurisdiction and other legal matters. Consider that officials only announced the investigation in March 2019, then went years without telling anyone what was going on or even if the case was dropped. (In fact, it was Her Majesty's Court of Appeals that informed us in 2021 that it was still ongoing, following another legal challenge.)

By the time the charges were brought, in February 2023, nearly 4½ years had passed. And the hearing itself didn't begin until Sept. 16, 2024, some 19 months later. That hearing lasted 12 weeks, until Dec. 6 of last year. As for why everything took so long, we can only speculate, but it's a combination of the aforementioned legal challenges, the sheer number, volume and complexity of the charges, and the difficulty in selecting the three-person, independent arbitration panel who will ultimately issue a judgm

articles.description: Roberto Mancini brushed off reports that his former club Manchester City have been found guilty by the Premier League of financial breaches allegedly committed during his time in charge of the club.
articles.headlineJa: 「自分には関係ない」元マンC監督のマンチーニ氏、有罪報道を一蹴
articles.descriptionJa: ロベルト・マンチーニ氏は、自身が指揮を執っていた期間に犯したとされる財務違反について、古巣のマンチェスター・シティがプレミアリーグから有罪と認定されたとする報道を一蹴しました。
articles.body:
Roberto Mancini brushed off reports that his former club Manchester City have been found guilty by the Premier League of financial breaches allegedly committed during his time as manager.

A source confirmed to ESPN on Friday that City were expected to be found guilty on the vast majority of 115 charges of financial breaches in their legal case with the Premier League.

- Man City verdict will leave a stain and stench on a Premier League era

- Man City vs. Premier League: 115 financial charges explained

- Returning Mancini accepts fans' jeers as Italy beaten by Belgium

Among the alleged breaches cited by the Premier League in 2023 were that City had failed to provide "full details of manager remuneration in its relevant contracts with its manager" between 2009 and 2013, the period in which Mancini was in charge and delivered City's first title in 44 years.

According to German publication Der Spiegel, Mancini is said to have at one point earned £1.45 million in a basic salary and £1.75 million as a consultant for a team controlled by City owner Sheikh Mansour in Abu Dhabi.

But speaking at a news conference in Türkiye on Sunday, the now-Italy coach questioned the reported verdict and said it was a matter for the club, not him.

"It's not an issue that concerns me," he said in Bursa ahead of Monday's UEFA Nations League fixture. "It's nothing new because this matter has been discussed for the last four or five years.

"Manchester City has not been found guilty, and the alleged double contract is not my concern. It's their issue, not mine."

In a statement on Friday, City didn't deny the guilty verdicts and said that the process "remains ongoing."

When contacted by ESPN, the Premier League said it wouldn't comment on a "private and confidential process."

In his own statement on Saturday, Man City chairman Khaldoon Al Mubarak said "nothing has changed" regarding the case, adding "our confidence and intent in proving the club's innocence is just as strong as when this began."

As well as the 2011-12 Premier League title, Mancini also led Man City to victory in the 2011 FA Cup final during his four seasons at the helm. 

He returned to take charge of Italy for a second time this summer.

The Associated Press contributed to this report.
